summary:
EmberLine is a web-based platform for exploring historical satellite observations of thermal anomalies across Indonesia. It brings together MODIS and VIIRS records from 2012–2026, harmonizing measurements to an Aqua MODIS reference scale. An interactive map, fire-history calendar, and seasonal analytics let users examine patterns across regions and time periods, with searchable filters and year, month, and FRP ranges.

The platform also highlights retrieval gaps and uncertainty so missing observations aren’t mistaken for zero activity. By making multi-sensor data easier to compare while clearly showing its limitations, EmberLine supports research and public understanding of historical fire patterns. It is an analytical and educational tool, not a real-time warning system or forecast.
details:
EmberLine turns historical MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations into an interactive view of thermal-anomaly patterns across Indonesia. Users can explore hotspot locations and density grids on a map, compare yearly or monthly activity in a calendar, and examine seasonal patterns using a 366-day climatology. Region, sensor, time, and FRP-range filters help focus the analysis.

To make observations from different sensors more comparable over time, EmberLine harmonizes VIIRS measurements to an Aqua MODIS reference scale while retaining raw sensor views. It distinguishes satellite retrieval gaps from valid zero readings and presents uncertainty and scientific limitations alongside the results. This helps users avoid treating missing data as evidence of no activity.

The browser-based application was developed with React, TypeScript, and Vite, using Leaflet for maps, ECharts for visualizations, and Framer Motion for animation. Its creative approach combines multi-sensor data, spatial exploration, and seasonal context in one interface. The team considered differences in sensor resolution and sensitivity, data gaps, uncertainty, accessibility, and responsive use. EmberLine aims to support research, planning, and public understanding of historical fire patterns; it is not a real-time alert or forecasting system.
